component.name: Clipsy
component.summary: Clipboard manager and history for Ubuntu

description.p: Clipsy remembers what you copy: text, rich text, images and files. Press a shortcut (Super+Shift+V by default) to open the history, search it, and paste any earlier item again.

ul.li: Search, filter by type, and pin favorite items
Keyboard-first: arrows, Enter, Ctrl+1 to 9 for quick paste
Light, dark and system themes
Works on Ubuntu's default desktop, on GNOME Wayland and Xorg
Local only: no network, no account, no telemetry

description.p: Windows parity with Linux, plus a new default shortcut.

ul.li: Windows: Win+Shift+V is now the default shortcut, like Ubuntu (falls back to Ctrl+Shift+V if Windows blocks it).
Windows: redesigned popup with delete, preview, hint bar and a resizable window.
Windows: clear history asks for confirmation inside the popup.
Windows: more settings (size limits, rich text) and the Clipsy logo everywhere.
Windows: images now paste into Paint, Word, browsers and terminals; text pastes into cmd and PowerShell.
Windows: Clipsy no longer opens a black command window.
Windows: Clipsy opens its history when you start it, and clicking the tray icon opens it too.
The website always shows the newest version and has a simpler light/dark button.
Pasting an image now works in terminals and tools such as Claude Code and opencode.
A redesigned welcome window that shows one screen at a time, with a clearer copy-command step.
Windows: fixed the startup error about the single-instance pipe and user SID.
A redesigned, more compact website.
Pasting into terminals is more reliable: Clipsy waits for the terminal to take focus before pasting.
More terminals are recognised, on X11 and on GNOME Wayland, and non-Latin keyboard layouts work.
New terminal_apps setting to paste with Ctrl+Shift+V in chosen apps.
A trash button next to the filter tabs clears one tab at a time, with an option to also remove pinned items.
A wider popup, and a new multi-page welcome screen.
Clicking an item pastes correctly in Warp and more terminals.

description.p: The filter tabs (All, Text, Images, Files, Pinned) select with one click on Wayland and Xorg.

ul.li: Wayland setup works with one command pasted into a Terminal, then one log out and back in.
Clearer setup steps, and the welcome window can be closed, moved and resized.
Old items are deleted automatically: unpinned items after 2 days and pinned items after 10 days by default. Both can be changed in Settings (1 day to 90 days, or never).
Files copied in the Files app on Wayland now show under the Files filter.
One click on an item pastes it everywhere, on Xorg and Wayland.

description.p: The GNOME extension setup command now works when pasted into a Terminal.
Fixes the setup command for the GNOME extension, which could fail with "does not exist" before logging out.

ul.li: Works on GNOME Wayland (Ubuntu's default desktop) via a small GNOME extension that Clipsy helps you turn on
New app icon
Easier to find in the App Center

description.p: Keeps running after the terminal that started it is closed. First stable release.
Snap package fixes: runs inside the strict snap sandbox, starts at login correctly.
First version: history, popup, settings and first-run welcome.
